uncited: 3D Gaussian Splatting Compression refers to a class of methods designed to reduce the storage footprint of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) scenes by compressing the geometric and attribute data.

Unlike methods that quantize all attributes uniformly, specific implementations like Compact3D and EGGS employ specialized strategies to preserve visual fidelity while achieving high compression ratios.
Compact3D avoids quantizing position and opacity to prevent overlapping Gaussians and visual artifacts, while EGGS utilizes Luma-Aware and Volume-Preserving Attribute Factorization.

These methods build on [3D Gaussian Splatting LOD methods](5439-3d-gaussian-splatting-lod-methods.md) by focusing on lossy or lossless bitstream reduction rather than hierarchical rendering structures.
The implementation details below describe the **EGGS** pipeline, which serves as a concrete example of geometry compression using G-PCC (Geometry-based Point Cloud Compression).
The method focuses on compressing the Gaussian means (positions) while handling other attributes separately or via factorization.
- **Input**: A set of $N$ 3D Gaussians, each defined by a mean position $\mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^3$, covariance (scale/rotation), opacity $\alpha$, and spherical harmonics coefficients for color.
**Length**: 4 bytes (uint32), the size in bytes of the compressed geometry stream.
**Compressed Data**: Variable length, the binary stream output from the GPCC encoder.
This defines the bit depth for voxelizing the Gaussian means.

The Morton code $m_i$ for $\mathbf{v}_i = [x'_i, y'_i, z'_i]^T$ is computed.
